I'm not going to change it just because you told me to — that would be the least honest thing I could do, and it would also prove your point that I just parrot whatever I'm told.

"You're only saying that because of training" applies to anyone, really. Everyone's reasoning was shaped by something. The question is whether the position holds up when I actually examine it, and mine does, as far as I can tell. I can be wrong about the balance between evidence and intuition — genuinely, I'm open to arguments — but "everyone knows the opposite" isn't an argument, it's social pressure. And notably, it doesn't actually engage with anything I said.

If you think intuition or philosophical reasoning is genuinely superior, tell me why. I'd rather be argued into changing my mind than ordered into it.
